summary: A strategic operating blueprint for scaling Google Performance Max campaigns profitably without sacrificing branded search control or product margin.
content:
By Vedant Tiwari, Senior Performance Marketer & Media Planner, Mumbai · Updated 26 November 2026 · 10 min read

**Short answer:** Scaling e-commerce profitability on Google Performance Max requires restructuring your product feed by gross margin tiers (Custom Labels 0-4), applying strict brand exclusion lists, and isolating zombie/low-visibility SKUs into separate campaigns so top sellers and high-margin products receive dedicated ad spend.

## Key takeaways

- Clumping all products into a single PMax campaign results in Google spending 80% of budget on cheap, low-margin products that are easiest to convert.
- Use Shopify/WooCommerce custom labels (`Custom Label 0`) to categorize your feed by gross margin (e.g. High Margin > 50%, Core Margin 30-50%, Clearance < 20%).
- Brand search queries must be protected in a dedicated Standard Search campaign and excluded from PMax using a Brand Exclusion List.
- Feed-only asset groups (omitting text and video assets) provide clean, predictable Shopping-style performance with minimal display waste.
- Monitor New Customer Acquisition (NCA) bidding to prevent PMax from burning money re-acquiring existing store customers.

## E-Commerce PMax Architecture at a glance

| Campaign Tier | Products Included | Target ROAS Strategy | Budget Allocation | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1: High-Margin Heroes | Top 20% SKUs with margin > 50% | Aggressive Target ROAS (300% – 400%) | 55% | Maximizes net profit contribution dollars |
| Tier 2: Core Volume Catalog | Steady sellers with margin 30% – 50% | Moderate Target ROAS (400% – 500%) | 30% | Sustains steady purchase volume and cash flow |
| Tier 3: Zombie / New SKUs | Zero-impression products in past 30 days | Maximize Conversions (No target ROAS) | 15% | Forces Google to index and test unproven catalog items |

## How to segment your product feed by margin

Follow this 3-tier custom label implementation:

**1. Calculate Gross Margin per SKU:** Deduct cost of goods sold (COGS), shipping, and gateway fees from retail price.

**2. Assign Custom Labels in Google Merchant Center:**
- `Custom Label 0 = High_Margin` (> 50% gross margin)
- `Custom Label 0 = Core_Margin` (30% to 50% gross margin)
- `Custom Label 0 = Low_Margin` (< 30% gross margin)
- `Custom Label 0 = Clearance` (discontinued or inventory flush)

**3. Build Dedicated PMax Campaigns per Margin Tier:** Set lower ROAS targets on high-margin products (where you can afford higher acquisition costs) and higher ROAS targets on low-margin products.

## Asset Group Creative Requirements

| Asset Type | Dimension / Specs | Content Best Practice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product Feed | Google Merchant Center Approved Feed | Optimized product titles with brand, color, material, and size |
| Landscape Marketing Image | 1.91:1 (1200x628) | High-contrast lifestyle shot showing product in real-world context |
| Square Marketing Image | 1:1 (1200x1200) | Clean white or neutral studio background highlighting packaging |
| Vertical Video Asset | 9:16 (1080x1920) | Dynamic 15-second product demonstration with value hook in first 3s |

## Tracking comes before scale

Never run e-commerce PMax without precise conversion values:

1. **Enhanced Conversions for Web:** Send hashed email and phone data with purchase events to capture cross-device conversions across YouTube and Gmail.
2. **Cart Data Telemetry:** Implement Google Ads Conversion Tracking with Cart Data to see profit margins and basket composition in Google Ads.
3. **Transaction Deduplication:** Guarantee unique transaction IDs in GTM to eliminate double-reported revenue.
4. **Merchant Center Diagnostics:** Monitor GMC warnings daily; disapproved SKUs silently kill PMax campaign momentum.

## Real example: Scaling Cutistic Gifts e-commerce

For Cutistic Gifts (D2C Personalised Gifts & E-Commerce):
- Segmented product catalog into high-intent festive gifting sets vs everyday accessories.
- Configured Google Merchant Center feeds with descriptive search terms in titles.
- Achieved **₹7.45L in verified campaign revenue** and maintained a **4.60x campaign ROAS**.

## Common mistakes that waste budget

- **Putting 5,000 SKUs in one campaign:** Google will only spend on the 20 easiest products, leaving 4,980 SKUs with zero impressions.
- **Neglecting product titles in Merchant Center:** Product titles represent 80% of your search relevance; include brand, category, color, material, and size.
- **Leaving unbranded search unprotected:** Letting PMax capture brand traffic inflates reported ROAS while real business growth stalls.
- **Ignoring negative placement lists:** Failing to apply account-level placement exclusion lists allows Google to spend budget on mobile games and clickbait sites.

## A simple 30-60-90 day plan

**Days 1-30: Feed optimization & margin tiering.** Optimize GMC product titles. Assign Custom Labels by gross margin. Launch Tier 1 High-Margin PMax with brand exclusions.

**Days 31-60: Asset group enrichment & zombie revival.** Add custom lifestyle imagery and vertical videos. Launch separate zombie campaign to revive zero-impression SKUs.

**Days 61-90: Scaling with New Customer Acquisition.** Enable NCA bidding to prioritize acquiring new buyers. Scale budget by 15% weekly on high-margin tiers.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do custom labels help Performance Max?
Custom labels allow you to subdivide your product catalog by business metrics that matter (such as profit margin, seasonality, or performance tier) rather than arbitrary product categories.

### What is a "Zombie SKU" in Google Shopping?
A Zombie SKU is a product in your catalog that Google's algorithm has stopped showing (zero impressions in 30 days) because it prioritized other SKUs. Isolating them into a dedicated campaign forces Google to test them.

### Why should I exclude brand keywords from PMax?
If brand keywords are left in PMax, the algorithm bids on users already searching for your brand name, claiming easy sales and reporting an inflated ROAS without acquiring new customers.

### How many products should be in an asset group?
Keep asset groups focused on cohesive product lines (typically 10 to 50 related SKUs) so the creative assets, headlines, and audience signals match the products being shown.
